title: Split-range control
physicalPurpose: Map one signed heat-balance demand into opposing unipolar valves without a control gap or simultaneous utility waste.
objective: Map one signed demand to opposing heating and cooling actuators.

simplifications: Local linear thermal balance from 72 through 88 degC
Constant installed valve gains and ideal requested-equals-applied positions
No valve stiction, pressure variation, transport delay or utility-temperature dynamics
Three deterministic equivalent plants isolate only split-range mapping

baseline.limitation: A dead zone removes authority near neutral while overlap consumes opposing utilities and drifts when their installed gains differ.

change.decision: Accept the mutually exclusive mapping only when installed-gain scaling balances local authority, zero demand closes both valves, and crossover and authority-loss evidence are bounded.

disturbances: Setpoint changes from 80 to 84 degC at 20.0 s
Setpoint changes from 84 to 76 degC at 80.0 s
Setpoint returns to 80 degC at 140.0 s
A separate restored run removes automatic authority

acceptance.window: complete 200-s run while both characterized valves exceed 0.1 percent
complete run with absolute demand at least 0.25 percent and both valves at most 0.1 percent
all samples with characterized signed demand below -1 percent
all samples in separate unavailable-authority run

abortPredicates: Any required signal is nonfinite, stale, forced, or has invalid quality
Any reactor temperature leaves 72 through 88 degC
Any valve request leaves 0 through 100 percent
Automatic authority, mapping identity, or restoration is lost
safety.restorationMode: Track signed demand to zero with controller setpoint aligned to measured temperature, close both utilities, and qualify valve feedback before restoring automatic authority.
safety.physicalApprovalRole: authorised reactor controls engineer and responsible process operator
simulationOnlyRestrictions: No physical heating or cooling valve is operated
Ideal valve requests are not physical installed-characteristic evidence
Physical split range requires reviewed utilities, valve fail positions, interlocks, pressure and temperature limits, tracking and explicit experiment approval

video.viewerOutcome: Map one signed temperature demand into characterized heating and cooling valves and explain the measured cost of dead zone and overlap.
requiredVisibleEvidence: all requested and applied valve pairs

learning.context: Three equivalent batch reactors use opposing hot-water and cooling-water valves with unequal local installed gains around 80 degC.
learning.reason: Unlike the simultaneously useful streams in ratio control, opposing utilities require one signed demand to select and sequence only the appropriate final element.
theory: A signed PI output changes valve authority at a declared split point; the mapper, not another PID, selects heating or cooling.
Dead zone removes neutral authority while overlap consumes both utilities and unequal installed gains create a net disturbance.
Installed-gain characterization scales cooling by two thirds so equal signed demand has equal local thermal effect.
learning.workedPrediction: At zero demand the overlap mapping opens both valves 4 percent and creates 0.08 degC/s net cooling; the characterized mapping closes both, and -20-percent demand maps to 13.33-percent cooling.
practicalPreparation: Verify Simulation evidence, all plant/controller/final-element identities, signs, units, requested/applied values, gains, mapping widths, sample time, quality, authority and limits.
Define event error, valve movement, gap and overlap exposure, utility throughput, crossover bump and settling eligibility before viewing results.
learning.baseline: Run exact four-point dead-zone and overlap mappings to retain their lost-authority and simultaneous-utility evidence.
learning.change: Use mutually exclusive neutral selection and scale cooling demand by the measured heating-to-cooling installed-gain ratio.
learning.comparison: Hold plant, initial state, signed PI tuning, setpoint sequence, timing, limits and seed equal while changing only mapping.
learning.validation: Require finite bounded values, no characterized overlap or gap, closed valves at zero and during authority loss, correct two-thirds cooling scale, and bounded neutral crossover.
learning.explanation: The final-element mapper changes effective loop dynamics; dead zone delays action, overlap wastes energy, and gain scaling balances local authority.
